text:
sam: Heads-up — procurement asked us to pick a booking window strategy for H100/H200/L40S ahead of Q2 forecasting. Need opinions on commit length vs flexibility. Key constraints: APAC H200 lead times ~12-16 weeks, EU supply tapering, L40S available for immediate burst but ~20-30% lower throughput per card.

ari: Could we do a hybrid? longer-term H200 reserve for steady base, H100 spot/burst for unpredictable peaks. Also consider convertible reservations (if vendor supports swapping) so we get flexibility. :thinking:

maria: Quick numbers from the throughput model: median project needs ~2.1k GPU-hrs/day baseline, seasonal peak +60% for onboarding spikes. If baseline on H200 (perf +40% vs H100), we save ~18% unit cost in tokens/sec. But H200 commit costs ~25% premium in RR pricing.

sam: thanks. can you paste the short table?

ari: Sure — rough sketch:
```
option, baseline perf, cost premium, lead time
H200 reserved, +40%, +25%, 12-16w
H100 reserved, +0%, 0%, 8-12w
L40S burst, -25% perf, -10% spot cost, immediate
Hybrid (H200 base + L40S burst), +15% effective, +5% net cost, 12-16w
```

maria: Important: network egress limits in APAC cluster mean effective throughput can drop if we overbook I/O heavy workloads. Would advise holding ~10% headroom for staging migrations.

nate: FYI, devops-bot shows current reservation pipeline: 3 pending H200 racks in us-west with ETA 2026-06-01; vendor holdbacks possible. Payload: `resv-2026-06-h200-usw` status: queued.

devops-bot: Reservation status update: queued -> vendor-confirmed expected by 1937800000. No cancellations yet.

jia: Two tradeoffs to surface to finance: (1) longer commits reduce $/GPU-hr but increase cost of forecast error, (2) convertible or exchangeable reservations reduce mismatch risk but have higher fees. I propose: run a 6-week sensitivity on booking windows (8w vs 16w vs 24w) and present expected regret (dollars) under three demand scenarios. I'll own the ask to Forecast team.

sam: Agreed. action items: ari/maria do 6-week sensitivity + update throughput model with APAC egress caps; nate confirm vendor flexibility on conversion; jia draft finance ask. We'll chat Wed. :thumbsup:

maria: one more note — if we go heavy H200, schedule a canary rollout in eu-west first (smaller queues) to validate perf assumptions before global traffic shift.

sam: Perfect. thanks all.
